actions.action: Check whether the bucket has drainage holes
Repot into a plastic nursery pot with drainage and use the bucket as a cachepot
Slide the plant out and inspect the roots
Trim mushy, brown or black roots with clean scissors
Repot in a chunky aroid mix of orchid bark, perlite and potting soil
Check the top 1-2 inches of soil and water thoroughly only when dry, letting the excess drain
Cut off badly damaged brown leaves or leaf parts
Move the plant to bright, indirect light near an east window or back from a south or west window
Resume diluted fertilizer once new healthy growth appears
If stems are rotting, cut above the damage and root healthy node cuttings in water

reason: The answer identifies dense wet soil, poor drainage and low light as the main problems, and its core advice (drainage, chunky aroid mix, more light) matches the repot that worked, with nothing harmful.
